newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen jittery on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen jittery on U.S. data.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks forecast to trade on U.S. economic statistics on Tuesday, starting with Q2 employment cost index before bell.
* Weaker gold bullion prices seen putting pressure on market.
Toronto stocks are likely to trade off a raft of U.S. economic statistics on Tuesday, beginning with the closely watched employment cost index before the open.
"The market in general is going to tee off the economic news today," one trader said.

The U.S. second quarter employment cost index matched economists' expectations, rising 0.8 percent compared to a 0.6 percent gain in the first quarter. "A negative start to the U.S. is expected and we'll will slip in sympathy," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie.
The next statistics to hurdle include Conference Board Consumer Confidence for July, which is forecast to rise to 130.4 from 129.6, and Johnson Redbook for the week of July 26.
In Canada, the June Industrial Product Price Index dipped 0.2 percent while the June Raw Materials Price Index fell 2.3 percent from May.
Market watchers also predicted weaker gold bullion prices would weigh heavily on Toronto's key gold group, pulling down the whole 300 Composite index. August gold prices on COMEX fell 1.80 to 327.70.
The index on Monday reached its 28th record close of the year, climbing 12.04 points to finish at 6792.31 and setting an intraday high of 6814.47.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* Prudential Steel Ltd posted second quarter earnings on Tuesday of C$0.82 a share versus year-earlier C$0.23 and increased its quarterly dividend to C$0.15 from C$0.125 a share. It also announced a three-for-one stock split.

* Abitibi-Conosolidated Inc, the world's largest newsprint maker by a two-to-one margin, is scheduled to post second quarter numbers. Analysts forecast an average estimate of C$0.14 a share compared to a year-earlier C$0.26.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
